notes:
Inbound via self-serve signup + trial credits. SMB D2C apparel + home goods. Main asks: product Q&A widget for PDPs, automated attribute enrichment (materials, fit, care), and better on-site search relevance. Wants quick rollout before Spring promo.

Call notes (2026-02-18, intro call with AE):
- Team: CTO (Maya R.), Head of Product (Logan S.), small eng team (2).
- Quote from CTO: "Need something that just works - low ops, predictable cost during flash sales."
- Current: Algolia for search, in-house rules for Q&A (poor coverage). Catalog ~12k SKUs, sparse attributes across legacy feeds.
- Traffic pattern: baseline 800-1,500 daily sessions; promo windows spike 3-5x for 6-12 hours (Black Friday-like but smaller). Expected peak requests to Q&A/search ~50-200 RPS during promos.
- Latency target for Q&A widget: <=300ms to keep UX snappy. Cost sensitivity: high - prefer self-serve hosted to avoid infra overhead.
- Security: SOC2 compliance preferred; no VPC/on-prem requirement.
- Data concerns: product text + images; they will not send PII. Ask about data retention and audit logging.

Technical notes:
- Interested in prefix/KV caching and batching for burst handling. Wants guidance on prompt templates and embedding strategy for catalog enrichment.
- Will provide sample catalog CSV (sent drive link) and example PDPs.
- SE asked to provide sample throughput/cost estimate and a minimal config for caching + rate limits.

Next steps agreed:
- AE to send pricing link + quickstart (done 2026-02-18).
- SE to share recommended prompt templates and a small code snippet for frontend widget (due 2026-02-22).
- Demo scheduled 2026-02-25 (product walkthrough + latency/cost discussion).
- 7-day POC request: integrate hosted API on staging, validate latency under burst, validate enrichment quality on 1k SKUs.

Risks/blockers:
- Budget: needs $/month approval from CFO for paid trial beyond credits.
- Data cleanup: attributes inconsistent - enrichment may need mapping work.
- Peak capacity: wants assurance hosted API handles brief spikes without large bill surprises.
